items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public officers law, in relation to personally identifiable information and certain researchers; and to amend the public health law, in relation to unlawful interference with research laboratory operations
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5731

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the public officers law, in relation
to personally identifiable information and certain researchers; and to
amend the public health law, in relation to unlawful interference with
research laboratory operations

PURPOSE:  To increase privacy protections related to the personally
identifiable and other similar information of certain researchers and
to establish penalties for the interference with research.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one amends subdivision 2 of section 87 of the public officers
law to add a specific exemption to the freedom of information law to
protect personally identifiable information or other information not
generally available to the public when such information is contained
in records relating to research.

Section two amends subdivision 2 of section 96 to the public officers
law by adding a new paragraph (e) which makes a similar and conforming
change to the personal privacy protection law.

Section three amends the public health law by adding a new section 506
which establishes the crime of unlawful interference with research
laboratory operations.

Section four establishes the effective date as immediately.

JUSTIFICATION:  New York is home to a number of world class biomedical
research institutions. The work being done in state is often at the
forefront of biomedical science and is quite literally saving lives.
Unfortunately, researchers across the country have found themselves
the target of individuals and groups who are opposed to the work they
are doing for any number of reasons Researchers have received
threatening letters, have been the victims of vandalism, cyber
harassment and, in the most egregious circumstances, they and their
families have been the victims of violence. The purpose of this
legislation is two-fold. First, it adds language to the freedom of
information law and the personal privacy protection law to ensure that
personal information or other generally non-public information is not
accessible. Second, it establishes penalties for unlawful interference
with research, creating a more cohesive mechanism by which to address
the criminal activity of those who seek to disrupt research, threaten,
harass or even harm researchers. A number of states, most notably
California, in the wake of a number of violent incidents, have taken
similar action in order to support and protect their researchers. New
York, as a leader in biomedical research, certainly should be
pro-active on this important issue.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: New bill

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: None.

EFFECTIVE DATE: Immediately.

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the public officers law, in relation
to the safety and security of a research laboratory; and to amend the
public health law, in relation to unlawful interference with research
laboratory operations

PURPOSE:

To increase safety and security protections related to the personally
identifiable and other similar information of certain researchers and
to establish penalties for the interference with research.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one amends subdivision 2 of section 87 of the public officers
law by adding a new paragraph n relating to research under the
auspicies of a research laboratory that if disclosed would jeopardize
the safety or security of a research laboratory, its employees, or
family members of its employees.

which establishes the crime of unlawful interference with research
laboratory operations.

Section three establishes the effective date as immediately.

of biomedical science and is quite literally saving lives.

B.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to unlawful interference with research laboratory operations
B.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5731B

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the public health law, in relation to
unlawful interference with research laboratory operations

PURPOSE:  To deny access to certain records concerning biomedical
research if it would endanger the life or safety of any person, or the
safety and security of a biomedical research laboratory.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Section one amends the public health law by adding a new
section 506 to deny access to records or portions concerning biomedical
research if such disclosure could endanger the life or safety of any
person or would be reasonably likely to endanger the security of such
biomedical research laboratory.

Section 2: Section two outlines an immediate effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:  New York is home to a number of world class biomedical
research institutions. The work being done in state is often at the
forefront of biomedical science and is quite literally saving lives.
Unfortunately, researchers across the country have found themselves the
target of individuals and groups who are opposed to the work they are
doing for any number of reasons Researchers have received threatening
letters, have been the victims of vandalism, cyber harassment and, in
the most egregious circumstances, they and their families have been the
victims of violence. This legislation would deny access to records
concerning biomedical research or biomedical teaching if such disclosure
could endanger the life or safety of any person or would be reasonably
likely to endanger the security of such biomedical research laboratory.
A number of states, most notably California, in the wake of a number of
violent incidents, have taken similar action in order to support and
protect their researchers. New York, as a leader in biomedical research,
certainly should be pro-active on this important issue.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: 2014: New bill

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: None.

EFFECTIVE DATE: Immediately
